change.title: 1972 opening sequence: arrival, identity, Birmingham estate, Frankfurt and New York
change.reason: Author-requested revision of the opening chronology. One atomic group keeps the identity conversion and causal references consistent. Review interpretations: Frankfurt arrival is proposed as 2 February, immediately after the Birmingham process; “Great Orome” is interpreted as Great Orme. The hotel name is retained exactly as requested as a story choice; its historical 1972 name and availability have not been verified. The car sold during estate settlement is left unspecified and is not identified as the wrecked accident vehicle. Lottery dates and banking services follow the supplied alternative-history account, not an independently verified historical reconstruction. No prize amount, estate value, bank-account opening date before the transfer, body-substitution mechanics or new family names are invented. December 1939 family background remains prose because structured story dates begin in 1972. The previous immediate claim of rapid wealth multiplication is replaced by the actual March 1 outcome: accounts opened and investing begun. All listed resulting records are authorized together on approval.

after.name: Adam Pleskot (original identity holder)
after.description: The original Adam Pleskot was nineteen years old and had been educated in Birmingham, where he lived with his Polish parents. His parents moved to the United Kingdom in December 1939 during World War II. Adam had graduated from high school. He and both parents died when their car fell off a cliff during a trip to Great Orme.

before.statement: Vincent gains time-travel powers at age nineteen in 2025 and operates in the past as Adam Pleskot. His foreknowledge remains secret.
